concepts.primary_text: My dentist gave me a $2,400 replacement quote for my upper plate. I walked home, opened the bathroom drawer, and looked at what was inside. Brushes with frayed bristles. Blue Polident boxes. Efferdent packets. Three years of receipts. My dentures smelled fresh for an hour after soaking, but by afternoon the yellow film was back. You could feel that slick film with your tongue. There is a big difference between clean and looks clean. I spent 40 years as a machinist working with close tolerances. When acrylic gets scratched by a toothbrush, bacteria and food particles crawl into micro-pores no bristle or fizzy tablet can touch. The surface looks rinsed, but the bacteria stay inside, rotting and staining the plate yellow. I spent three weeks looking into ultrasonic cleaners. Most of them are cheap plastic tubs with a vibrating motor. In a 90-day lab test of seven leading pods, six left live bacteria on dentures overnight. The only one that passed was the DentalPULSE ultrasonic cleaner. It runs at 42,000 Hz. That creates microscopic bubbles that implode against the acrylic and pull out the bacteria, biofilm, and yellow stains that brushing misses. You put in tap water, press the button, and walk away. In one 5-minute cycle, it shuts off automatically. The first time I used it, the water in the tank turned cloudy brown. That was everything soaking in blue water had left behind for years. My dentures have not looked this white or felt this smooth since the day I got them. If you are tired of wasting money on boxes of tablets that only mask the smell, try DentalPULSE. It comes with a 120-day money-back guarantee. If it does not get your dentures genuinely clean, you get every dollar back.
